ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of shareholders, managers, UBOs and counterparties against Luxembourg CLERP lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and PEP databases (e.g., World-Check). Enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons and for charter broker counterparties under Law of 12 November 2004. Compliance documentation must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin script; statutes and RCS filings are in French, German, or Luxembourgish. Names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet, must be linguistically acceptable in all three official languages, and must not be misleading or contrary to public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of refusal, the applicant may request a written opinion from the LBR and then file a motion for reconsideration within one month. An administrative appeal (recours en réformation) may be lodged with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of the refusal decision. Pending appeal, the applicant may re-file a new name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office for an SARL. The company must maintain a physical registered office (siège social) in Luxembourg, with full administrative and operational substance. For a licensed air cargo charter broker, a local operational address is mandatory; shared office and administrative service providers may be used but must support actual decision-making and record custody.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Medium: 25% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection by the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works or AMLD supervision for compliance with commercial substance requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Companies Act 1915), as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016; SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 to 710-25, Article 710-3 (mandatory contents of the constitutive deed), Article 710-24 (annual general meeting and accounts); RCS and RESA governance under the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filing via the MyLBR/eJustice portal; official publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive deed / Articles of Association ('Statuts' / 'Acte constitutif'), executed either before a Luxembourg notary or as a private deed on the ministerial standard model approved under the Law of 23 July 2016, accompanied by the RCS incorporation questionnaire.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum subscribed capital is EUR 12,000 (Article 710-1, Companies Act 1915 as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016), fully subscribed by quotas of equal nominal value; at least 25% of the nominal value of each cash quota (aggregate minimum EUR 3,000 on the statutory minimum capital) must be paid up at formation by deposit into a blocked 'compte de consignation' with a Luxembourg credit institution, evidenced by an 'attestation de blocage'; the unpaid balance must be settled within five years of incorporation; contributions in kind require a valuation report by an independent réviseur d'entreprises; blocked funds are released only upon completion of RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the founders acting as the constitutive assembly: (1) The draft Articles of Association are approved; the company is formed under the Law of 10 August 1915 as a Société à Responsabilité Limitée with share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and declared paid up at the legal minimum of EUR 3,000. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address, L-XXXX, Luxembourg], being an effective establishment in Luxembourg. (3) [Name] is appointed sole gérant, with full powers to file the constitutive deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers, publish in RESA, obtain the establishment authorization, register for taxation and social security, and open and operate banking accounts; all prior acts performed on behalf of the not-yet-formed company are hereby ratified.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate and income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for Luxembourg VAT; Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu as the integrated corporate and tax registration portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL must first be incorporated before a notary and filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS). Upon RCS registration, the ACD automatically assigns a Luxembourg national tax identification number (NIF) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes. For VAT, the SARL, or any foreign taxable person making taxable supplies in Luxembourg, must file a VAT registration application with the AEDT, providing its RCS excerpt, articles of association, proof of Luxembourg business address, identity of directors/managers, and, where required, a Luxembourg VAT representative. The AEDT then issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits). Non-established foreign suppliers have no turnover threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT before making their first taxable supply in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box election. A SARL is mandatorily classified as a fully taxable corporate entity subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. Relevant elective mechanisms available include the Luxembourg VAT grouping regime (assujetti unique) for VAT consolidation, and the group taxation regime under Article 164bis LIR for resident companies holding at least 95% direct or indirect participations. Hybrid mismatch elections are not discretionary; Luxembourg implements the EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules, and no substantive pass-through election is available to a SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implemented under the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA) in conformity with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General Luxembourg small-business VAT exemption threshold: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) for supplies of goods and services by established taxable persons. A SARL below this threshold may apply for small-business exemption but may also voluntarily opt into VAT. Non-established foreign suppliers engaged in taxable supplies in Luxembourg are required to register with no turnover threshold. For intra-EU distance sales of goods into Luxembourg, the domestic distance-selling threshold is EUR 100,000 per calendar year, subject to the EU One Stop Shop (OSS) mechanism and any lowering of the general EU threshold under current Digital Age proposals.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or fiscal stamping system for domestic B2B VAT. Electronic invoicing is mandatory in the B2G sector: suppliers to Luxembourg public authorities must issue EN 16931-compliant structured e-invoices through PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 via an interoperable access point. For private-sector B2B transactions, e-invoicing is permitted under EU rules but is not required as a tax clearance condition. No API-based emission of invoices to the AEDT is mandated today; however, Luxembourg is aligning with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposals, which will introduce structured e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements in the future.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically exported from Luxembourg or another EU Member State to non-EU destinations are zero-rated for Luxembourg VAT where the supplier holds conclusive evidence that the goods left the EU within the prescribed statutory period. For an air cargo charter broker under ISIC 5229, the following are eligible for 0% VAT: (i) international transport of goods to or from a third territory; (ii) transport of goods between EU Member States; and (iii) ancillary services, including loading, unloading, handling, and brokerage/commission services, provided that they are directly linked to, and physically/contractually connected with, the international transport of goods and are supplied to the international transport customer. Pure air cargo charter brokerage commissions arranging the carriage of goods from Luxembourg or another EU country to a non-EU destination therefore qualify for zero-rating, while purely domestic or non-transport-related services remain subject to Luxembourg VAT at the standard rate of 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: electronic Single Administrative Document or equivalent export declaration in EU customs systems, including the customs office of export and movement reference number confirming dispatch from the EU
Air Waybill (AWB): master and/or house air waybill evidencing carriage of cargo from the EU to the non-EU destination and identifying shipper, consignee, and route
Bill of Lading or multimodal transport document, where sea, road, or rail transport is used in whole or part of the international movement
Commercial invoice and underlying charter party agreement, brokerage contract, or commission note evidencing the supply and the agreed consideration
Bank payment proof or Inward Remittance Certificate: SWIFT confirmation or bank statement showing receipt of foreign currency or EUR payment from the non-resident principal or customer
Export movement and transit documentation, including customs transit declarations and delivery confirmation from the destination customs territory
Packing list and certificate of origin, where required by the importing country or the customer's customs formalities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg AEDT may retroactively disallow export zero-rating where the taxpayer fails to produce complete and coherent documentation proving that the goods were physically removed from the EU or that the services were directly connected with international cargo transport. Recharacterized supplies attract Luxembourg VAT at 17% with interest for late payment from the date the tax would have been due. In cases of fraud or material serious misconduct, Luxembourg law permits assessments within an extended limitation period of up to 10 years, administrative fines proportional to the evaded VAT, criminal sanctions including imprisonment for VAT fraud, and joint and several liability of directors or statutory representatives of the SARL. Officers of a Luxembourg SARL may also face disqualification proceedings and seizure of corporate assets in the case of intentional participation in a zero-rating evasion scheme.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB), with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the prudential supervisor for regulated financial activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a member of the European Union and the eurozone, maintains full capital-account and current-account convertibility in accordance with Articles 63 and 64 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Profit remittance and dividend distributions are subject only to standard corporate withholding tax procedure (15% domestic rate reduced by tax treaties, participation exemption or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where applicable) and are not subject to exchange-control approval. The euro is fully convertible; no surrender requirements or central bank authorization are imposed on current or capital transactions for residents. Administrative formalities may include the completion of the CSSF/BCL balance-of-payments reporting (BOP) framework for movements exceeding thresholds, but these are statistical, not restrictive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Luxembourg. Air cargo charter brokering receivables denominated in foreign currency (e.g., USD) may be retained externally, converted at commercial market rates, or used directly for operational and settlement purposes. For statistical balance-of-payments reporting, resident companies must declare individual cross-border payments in euro and foreign currencies to the BCL under the CSSF/BCL BOP regulation (Regulation EEE 2408/92 and national RGD 27 May 1997), but no surrender or forced conversion to EUR applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency current account) plus Foreign Currency Settlement Sub-Accounts (USD, EUR); Capital Escrow Account may be established for charter-related cargo security deposits if contractually required.

Operational Account (multi-currency) and Dedicated Escrow/Security Deposit Account for trade counter-party performance guarantees; Capital Escrow Account available for specific structured disbursement arrangements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Société Générale Bank & Trust S.A. Luxembourg
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade Cash Management Package; Capital Escrow Account for consignment/third-party charter fund handling.
Operational Account with dedicated cross-border payment routing (SWIFT and Fedwire); Capital Escrow Account available.
Operational Account for treasury liquidity concentration and FX hedging purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium—viable only for settlement of client receivables/payables in currencies without unlicensed restrictions under a Luxembourg or EU-passported Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence (e.g., under PSD2). Legal constraints: (i) the EMI cannot grant credit or hold client funds longer than 180 days unless client elects deposit; (ii) corporate cash management limits mean EMIs usually cannot support large air-cargo charter broker fund flows without a sponsoring credit institution; (iii) CSSF treats EMIs as high-risk for collective investment-like or escrow flows, requiring robust AML/KYC and transaction monitoring; (iv) Fedwire membership is generally unavailable for EMIs, so USD-clearing requires correspondent bank sponsorship. Onboarding viability: Low for primary treasury accounts; Medium for ancillary payment processing or merchant settlement platforms.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require the authorised signatories (preferably at least two directors including the ultimate beneficial owner if a natural person) to attend a physical in-person interview at the bank premise or at a Luxembourg notary/embassy for the initial onboarding. Remote video-onboarding (via digital identity verification) is admitted for simpler corporate structures and lower-risk activities, but for an air cargo charter broker classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, local banks typically insist on a physical visit of the board members or an appointed corporate officer with power of attorney. If the SARL has no office in Luxembourg, the bank may require physical attendance by the managers (gérants) and proof of substance (lease agreement, local VAT/tax presence).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Complex ownership chain with multiple intermediate Luxembourg SARLs or foreign holding vehicles obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational chart with legal entity identifiers (LEIs), notarised articles of association for each intermediary, current certificate of registered office, register of shareholders, register of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE) extract, CVs of directors, and a written narrative of the corporate purpose demonstrating the air cargo charter brokerage operational logic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Incomplete documentary proof of underlying commercial contracts (charter agreements, aircraft lease agreements, fuel purchase contracts, sub-agent arrangements).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly signed charter framework agreements and purchase orders, invoices received/issued, evidence of aircraft operator certifications (AOC), insurance certificates (liability/hull), slat of charter programme cash-flow forecasts, bank reference letters from counterparties, and an annual audited financial statement if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Unusual or disproportional transaction activity for an air cargo charter broker, such as large payments to tax-haven jurisdictions, rapid back-to-back movements without commercial justification, or significant cash equivalents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level ledger with underlying voyage dossier, Air Waybill numbers, freight invoices, customs declarations, carrier settlement statements, fuel and navigation charges, applicable sanctions screening matrix, a compliance policy with UAE/UN/OFAC exclusion list screening procedures, and a written description of the counterparty due-diligence process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Insufficient substance to support being a Luxembourg treasury and payment agent for the group.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance dossier comprising lease agreement for local office or virtual office with mail handling and meeting room, employment contracts for at least one local administrator/compliance officer, minutes of board meetings held in Luxembourg, VAT registration certificate, and annual financial statements (or projected P&L for the first 18 months) demonstrating the SARL's operational reality.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Equity injections and shareholder loans must be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 or Fedwire with unambiguous purpose codes and remittance information. For Luxembourg, use the EU Balance of Payments (BOP) codes: for direct investment equity — 11010 (equity capital); for shareholder loans — 12010 (loans from parent); for trade/miscellaneous operating payment — 10000 services. The receiving bank will require the underlying instrument (share subscription agreement, loan facility agreement) and the CSSF/BCL BOP declaration will be made automatically via the bank. State the full legal name and SARL 'LU' Vat number (LU + n° d'identification fiscale) in the remittance information. Wire format must include IBAN for EUR shipments; for USD, ensure the ABA routing number of the intermediate correspondent is provided. The transaction reference must include the charter invoice number and the statement 'AIR CARGO CHARTER BROKERAGE — OPERATIONAL FUNDING'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer for all EUR and USD outbound trade disbursements (charter payments, fuel, crew, insurance, landing fees); (ii) Commercial letters of credit (L/C) under UCP 600 for high-value sub-charter transactions requiring documentary comfort, especially when acting as intermediary between aircraft operator and shipper; (iii) SEPA CT and SEPA Instant for eurozone counterparties; (iv) Fedwire for same-day USD priority disbursements requiring immediate value; (v) Correspondent banking through one of the tier-1 banks' downstream correspondent network (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas Fortis US branch or JP Morgan/Citi). Training: all outbound MT103s should include a structured reference with contract or flight number, and for USD-funded disbursements, use the FX pre-booked instruction to avoid settlement risk. For high-volume payables, ensure the bank offers a file-based bulk payment service with ISO 20022 camt.053 reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (EURUSD, EURGBP, EURCHF) with maturities up to 12 months under an ISDA or bank FX master agreement

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) limited to illiquid or restricted-convertibility currencies (e.g., certain African or Middle-Eastern currencies) where required for charter-party settlements; permissible under national law but subject to bank counterparty credit limits
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between EUR and USD for aligning legacy charter receivables or aircraft financing cash flows
FX Options (plain vanilla European puts/calls) for protecting budgeted charter prices against unfavourable exchange-rate movements
Foreign Exchange Swap/FX Swap (Swap Next/Swap Spot) for temporary treasury liquidity conversion between USD and EUR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) approved by the shareholders' meeting and filed/published through the Luxembourg Business Registers electronic filing portal (eLBR/RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting within 6 months of financial year-end; RCS filing within 1 month of approval and no later than 31 July for a calendar-year SARL (7-month statutory limit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS late-filing penalty of EUR 250; failure to file for three consecutive financial years triggers ex officio strike-off/administrative dissolution procedure (radiation d'office) and personal liability of the gérants for resulting damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership confirmation (mise à jour annuelle au Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) confirming the register data of all individual beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: at least once per calendar year; any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 500 up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years for fraudulent or knowingly false declarations; non-compliance also blocks notarial share transfer deeds and RCS formalities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct corporate tax return (combined declaration for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax) for the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg direct-tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; the ACD ordinarily grants an administrative extension to 31 December of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; administrative late-filing penalties up to EUR 25,000 under the General Tax Law; discretionary estimated assessments and enforced collection procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory auditor's report (rapport du réviseur d'entreprises agréé) annexed to the annual accounts when the SARL exceeds the small-undertaking thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) as annex to the annual accounts filing; submitted to the shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Report signed and issued before the shareholders' meeting held within 6 months of the financial year-end; filed with the annual accounts within 1 month of approval and by 31 July for calendar-year SARLs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-appointment of a réviseur d'entreprises when legally required renders the annual accounts non-conforming, exposes the gérants to civil/criminal liability, and may trigger RCS rejection and penalty proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé is compulsory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4,400,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,800,000; average headcount greater than 50. Small SARLs are exempt unless shareholders holding at least 10% of the capital request an audit; the ISIC 5229 air-cargo charter broker business license does not by itself impose an audit duty.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on undertakings (Commercial Code Title II), transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated or listed undertakings, so the SARL's statutory annual accounts must be prepared in EUR under Luxembourg GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an RBE declaration and confirm it at least once per calendar year regardless of ownership changes, reporting any shareholding transfer or change in the nature/extent of beneficial ownership within one month. SARL share transfers require a notarially or privately signed transfer deed, are opposable to third parties only after RCS registration, and must be mirrored in the register of members and in the annual RBE confirmation filed via the LBR authenticated eSpace by the gérant or registered agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder meetings and management decisions
Register of share transfers (registre des transferts de parts sociales)
Beneficial-owners RBE file and supporting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 4,900 per annum (approx. EUR 1,100 - 4,500) for a professional registered-office/domiciliation and corporate agent mandate in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - 21,500 per engagement (approx. EUR 5,000 - 20,000) for a statutory audit of a small-to-medium operating SARL; payable only if the Luxembourg GAAP audit thresholds are exceeded or an audit is validly requested by minority shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate for Luxembourg City (17.00% corporate income tax 'IRC' + 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC equal to 1.19% + municipal business tax of 6.75%); the aggregate rate ranges from approximately 20% to 27% depending on the commune of establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays; preferential regimes available: (i) participation exemption providing 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (>=10% or acquisition cost >= EUR 1.2 million, held for at least 12 months); (ii) IP Box regime granting an 80% exemption of net intellectual property income, producing an effective rate of approximately 4.99%; (iii) notional interest deduction on documented new equity contributions, with an annually published rate; (iv) EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive transposition providing 100% exemption for qualifying EU/EEA corporate parents.
